# PR #3578: Patch: an AI decision cut short by the clock still weighs the opponent's reply and every sampled world

Closes #3498

## What changed

When a host's clock stopped a decision while the beam was still exploring, the clock also refused every node after it. No finalist got a reply, and each was scored on one sampled world only. Now every host with a clock also fires an earlier **wrap-up**. The wrap-up stops only the beam, so the reply and the other worlds still run until the hard stop.

- **`crates/ai`**
  - New constant `AI_WRAP_UP_SHARE = 0.6` in `config.rs`. `wrap_up_after_ms(limit_ms)` is the only place the share is applied.
  - `AiOptions.wrap_up` is a second callback beside `should_stop`.
  - The beam's slice of the node counter (`create_wrap_up_counter`) polls the wrap-up before each of its nodes, once it has drawn `root_branching + 1` nodes. When it fires, the slice refuses further nodes and reports `stoppedBy: clock`.
  - `beam_search_with` then calls `counter.end_exploring()`, so the lines it cut short can still end their turn and be replied to.
  - `SearchStats` gains `replied` and `worldsScored`, and `Decision::fell_short()` marks a searched decision that left a sampled world unscored.
  - `plan` now takes `&mut AiOptions`: with one more argument it would have hit clippy's limit of 7.
- **Hosts**
  - The wasm core has a private `SearchClock`. `ai_decide` and `bot_decide` derive the wrap-up from the time left at the call, which covers the practice AI, dungeon fights through the practice driver, and the browser's bots. With no deadline it reads no clock, so the C module is unaffected.
  - The server's `spawn_bot` (ladder bots) and the Duos `AiJob::ask` pass one too.
  - `bots::decide`, `DecideJob::run` and `boundary::decide` take the wrap-up beside `should_stop`. The bots' concession check still uses only the hard stop.
- **Reporting:** `cargo jackioh think` prints `replied`, `worldsScored` and a "fell short" line. The timing gate's lines carry `replied`, `worldsScored` and `fellShort`; it reports them but fails nothing on them.
- **Spec and docs:** §9.9's Budgets paragraph, new ruling `spec/rulings/R3498000.md`, `spec/pending/3498.md`, SURFACE §9 and §10.1, the `crates/ai`, `crates/wasm` and `crates/shared` READMEs, and the `SearchStats` type in `apps/web/src/wire/ai.ts`.

With no clock, or with a wrap-up that never fires, every decision takes the same nodes as before.

## How I tested it

- **`cargo test -p jackioh-ai --test ai r3498000`**: 5 passed. On a fake clock with N = half the no-clock decision's nodes:
  - wrap-up at poll N, hard stop later: `replied > 0`, `worldsScored == 3`, not fell short;
  - only the hard stop at poll N: `replied == 0`, `worldsScored == 1`, fell short (today's behaviour);
  - wrap-up and hard stop both at N: still no reply, one world;
  - a wrap-up that never fires decides exactly as with no clock;
  - a wrap-up that fires at the first poll still plays a searched move on all 3 worlds;
  - a counter unit test.

  With the `end_exploring()` call commented out, the main test fails with `replied: 0`.
- **`cargo test -p jackioh-ai --lib --test ai`**: 27 and 812 passed.
- **Other crates' tests** all passed:
  - `jackioh-shared` (with testkit), including the new `r3498000_a_bots_wrap_up_never_fired_decides_as_none_and_one_fired_at_once_still_plays`;
  - `jackioh-wasm-core --lib`, including the new `SearchClock` test;
  - `jackioh-wasm-c` (17);
  - `jackioh-tools … think` (7);
  - `jackioh-server` (with testkit).
- **Checks:** `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean. `cargo jackioh spec check` printed "1875 rulings, 4846 proofs, …: ok". `cargo jackioh classify --base origin/main --claims` printed `classify: Internal`.
- **Gate:** `cargo jackioh gate --shard 1/1` on this build and on a build of the base commit:
  - `[gate ai-vs-random] 19 wins`, `[gate ai-vs-greedy] 16 wins`, `[gate hard-vs-easy] 20 wins`, 0 search panics, on both builds;
  - the three per-game result files are byte-identical;
  - the perf and pinned decisions spend the same nodes on both (408, 150, 150, 1005, 324, 381);
  - the gate passes.
- **Web:**
  - `sh scripts/build-wasm.sh` succeeded;
  - `vitest run --project web --changed origin/main …`: 242 files and 4767 tests passed;
  - `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck` and eslint on the two touched TS files exit 0.

## Decisions the issue left open

- **Sub-counter, not a new stop reason.** The wrap-up stops only the beam's sub-counter and reports `StoppedBy::Clock`. I rejected a new `StoppedBy` variant (it would change the wire's three values) and a `should_stop` that is told the phase.
- **A floor before the first poll.** The wrap-up is first polled after `root_branching + 1` beam nodes. Without it, a wrap-up that fired before the beam would leave no line and the decision would fall back.
- **`end_exploring` only lifts the wrap-up's refusal.** It does not lift a budget cap: doing that too would change decisions made with no clock.
- **`replied` counts only passed or yielded lines.** `replied.len()` would also count lines scored statically without a reply.
- **The share is applied in Rust.** I rejected passing it from TypeScript (CLAUDE.md rule 9).
- **The gate only reports a short decision.** It does not fail on one, since the gate's search has no clock.

## Departures from the plan

- `crates/shared/tests/bots_boundary.rs` also needed the new argument (`None, None`).
- I shortened the shared test's name to fit rustfmt's width. Its wrap-up also counts polls, to prove it reaches the search.
- A `type ClockPoll` alias in the wasm core, which clippy's `type_complexity` asked for.
- The `think` test also checks that a decision with no clock does not fall short.

## For a reviewer to look at twice

- **The 0.6 share has not been tested.** It is a judgement; nobody has run a clocked strength screen, and CI cannot run one.
- **Wide boards already fall short with no clock.** The new stats show that the gate's two wide boards report `"replied":0,"worldsScored":2,"fellShort":true` under the 150-node budget that fat states get. The node budget runs out before the reply, with no clock involved, so this is old behaviour the new stats now reveal. It may deserve its own issue; I did not change it.
- **Small budgets can hide a refused reply.** `fell_short` reads `worldsScored < determinizations`, so a budget with a single world never shows as short.
- **One network call.** While checking `origin/main`, I ran `git fetch --dry-run` once by mistake. It was read-only and changed nothing locally.

````text
# #3498: Patch: an AI decision cut short by the clock still weighs the opponent's reply and every sampled world
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

The practice AI has 3 seconds to think in the browser. On a phone or a slow laptop, its biggest decisions run out of time while it is still exploring. When that happens it skips the two checks that keep it out of bad trades:

- it no longer imagines your swing back;
- it judges its move on one guess of your hidden cards instead of three.

So it plays worst on exactly the busy boards where it matters most, and only on slower devices. Once this is built, it stops exploring a little early so that it always has time left for those checks. Ladder bots, dungeon enemies and the co-op AI team think on a clock too and gain the same.

## Why

- **The reserve is counted in nodes, not time.** `crates/ai/src/decide.rs:475-486` gives the beam search all but a reserve of nodes, `reserve = (remaining / 2).min(finalist_count * per_finalist)`. The reserve pays for the finalists' scores after the opponent's reply (`reply_score`, `decide.rs:517-523`) and on every other sampled world (`decide.rs:538-557`).
- **When the clock fires, everything after it is refused.**
  - `crates/ai/src/simulate.rs:129-137`: once `should_stop` fires, the root counter is marked `StoppedBy::Clock` and every later `take()` returns false.
  - So `reply_score` returns None at once (`crates/ai/src/reply.rs:547-549`) and `replied` stays empty.
  - The finalists keep their beam scores from world 0 only (`decide.rs:524-533`), and the loop over the other worlds breaks on its first line.
- **This happens on ordinary devices.**
  - R2575000: "In a browser, 600 nodes took 0.6–0.9 s." The budget is now 1,200 nodes (`AI_BUDGET`).
  - `docs/polish/3-ai.md:1679-1680` puts a mid-range phone at three to five times slower than that.
  - The cap is `PRACTICE_AI_CLOCK_MS` = 3,000 (`crates/shared/src/config.rs:1990`).
  - Ladder bots stop at `BOT_DECISION_DEADLINE_MS` = 4,000 (`config.rs:955`), on the server's quarter of a CPU.
- **The reply is worth a lot.** `docs/polish/3-ai.md:1619-1627` measured it at 174 against 193 wins of 300 against greedy.
- **No gate sees this path.** The quality gates and the sweep count nodes, not time (§9.9, Budgets).

## Proposal

- **Give the beam an earlier stop.** `AiOptions` gains a wrap-up callback (or the clock callback learns which phase is asking).
  - The host fires it at a named share of its limit, a new constant in `crates/ai/src/config.rs`.
  - The beam's sub-counter stops on it; the reply and the other worlds stop only at the hard limit.
- **Report the shortfall.** `SearchStats` gains how many finalists were replied and on how many worlds they were scored. The timing gate and `cargo jackioh think` can then report a decision that fell short.
- **No clock, no change.** The gates, the sweep and the server's fold of a practice claim (R2560000) decide bit for bit as today.
- **Every host passes the wrap-up:** the practice worker, the dungeon fight, the ladder bots and the Duos AI team. §9.9's Budgets paragraph describes it.

## Where it lands

- `crates/ai/src/decide.rs`, `simulate.rs`, `types.rs` (`SearchStats`) and `config.rs`
- The practice host's clock in `crates/shared`, the wasm binding, and the server's bot and Duos callers
- `docs/v0.3.0/SURFACE.md`; spec §9.9 (`spec/09-architecture.md`)
- Tests in `crates/ai/tests/ai/search.rs`, beside the fake clock that counts polls (about line 1458)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With a fake clock that trips the wrap-up at poll N and the hard stop later, the finalists are scored after the reply on every sampled world, as `SearchStats` shows.
- [ ] The same test with only the hard stop at poll N reproduces today's behaviour (no reply, one world), so the test fails without the change.
- [ ] With no clock, every existing AI test decides the same, and `cargo jackioh gate` folds to the same hashes.
- [ ] The new share is a named constant (CLAUDE.md rule 9) and §9.9 describes it. If it settles something §9.9 does not, it has a ruling note.

## Size and risks

Medium in size, **hard** difficulty: the AI plus its hosts across several crates.

- On a slow device the beam explores a little less, in exchange for the reply the measurement above values more.
- The wasm binding and SURFACE.md change.
- Duos and the ladder bots share this path, so their tests must stay green.

   /// None for `deadline_ms <= 0`: no clock is read (the C module's `no_clock`).
   struct SearchClock { deadline_ms: f64, wrap_up_ms: f64, now_ms: fn() -> f64 }

   impl SearchClock {
       fn begin(deadline_ms: f64, now_ms: fn() -> f64) -> Option<SearchClock> {
           if deadline_ms <= 0.0 {
               return None;
           }
           let began = now_ms();
           let left_ms = (deadline_ms - began).max(0.0) as i64;
           Some(SearchClock { deadline_ms, wrap_up_ms: began + jackioh_ai::wrap_up_after_ms(left_ms) as f64, now_ms })
       }
       fn should_stop(&self) -> bool { (self.now_ms)() >= self.deadline_ms }
       fn wrap_up(&self) -> bool { (self.now_ms)() >= self.wrap_up_ms }
   }

   /// `decide`'s two callbacks: none without a clock.
   fn clocked<'a>(
       clock: Option<&SearchClock>,
       stop: &'a dyn Fn() -> bool,
       wrap: &'a dyn Fn() -> bool,
   ) -> (Option<&'a dyn Fn() -> bool>, Option<&'a dyn Fn() -> bool>) {
       match clock {
           Some(_) => (Some(stop), Some(wrap)),
           None => (None, None),
       }
   }

The practice AI has 3 seconds to think in the browser. On a phone or a slow laptop, its biggest decisions run out of time while it is still exploring. When that happens it skips the two checks that keep it out of bad trades:

## Risks

- **Determinism.** With `wrap_up: None` the counter takes today's path, and `end_exploring` does nothing without a wrap-up. The new stats enter no hash, and `#[serde(default)]` still reads old JSON. No pure crate reads a clock.
- **The C module.** `begin` returns before it reads `now_ms`, so `no_clock` is never called.
- **Time.** The remaining 40% pays for the endTurns, the reply and two more worlds: about 55 nodes on `mid_game`, more on a wide board. The hard stop still bounds it.
- **Churn.** Four signatures change (`bots::decide`, `DecideJob::run`, `boundary::decide`, `plan`), and every `AiOptions` literal does too. The compiler lists any that are missed.
